title: Elephant Toothpaste
description: Create a massive foam eruption using hydrogen peroxide, yeast, and dish soap. The catalyst reaction releases oxygen rapidly, creating towering foam columns.

title: Non-Newtonian Oobleck
description: Mix cornstarch and water to create a substance that's both solid and liquid. Punch it and it's hard — dip slowly and it flows like water.

title: Rain in a Jar
description: Simulate rainfall in a jar. Layer hot and cold water, then add shaving cream as clouds and food coloring that falls like raindrops.

title: Lava Lamp
description: Make a working lava lamp with oil, water, Alka-Seltzer, and food coloring. The gas bubbles carry colored water up and down in mesmerizing blobs.

title: Static Electricity Butterfly
description: Create a paper butterfly that appears to fly using static electricity. A balloon or PVC pipe makes it dance in mid-air.

title: Crystal Garden
description: Grow colorful crystal formations over several days using silicate solutions and metal salts. Each salt creates a different colored 'plant'.

title: Levitating Pencil
description: Make a magnet float in mid-air with nothing but a pencil. Slide two ring magnets onto a sharpened pencil with like poles facing — the second one hovers, held up purely by magnetic repulsion.
safetyLevel: Safe (magnets are strong — keep away from phones and credit cards)

title: Splitting Water with Electricity
description: Electrolysis: run a 9V battery through salt water and watch it split into hydrogen and oxygen bubbles. Collect both gases in test tubes — you'll get exactly twice as much hydrogen, proving water is H₂O.
safetyLevel: Supervision required — no open flames, don't inhale the gas

title: Dancing Milk Rainbow
description: Drop food coloring into whole milk, then touch one drop of dish soap to the surface — the colors explode and swirl for minutes. The soap breaks the milk's surface tension and races through its fat molecules, creating real fluid currents you can watch.

title: Homemade Magnetic Fluid
description: Build your own ferrofluid — a liquid that stands up in spiky towers when you bring a magnet near. Mix iron oxide powder into vegetable oil and watch it defy gravity, forming sharp peaks that follow the magnet.
safetyLevel: Supervision required — don't eat or drink it, wash hands after
